name: Cray-1 vector registers
note: 8 vector registers x 64 elements x 64 bit; a vector-length register sets how many elements an instruction processes; chaining forwards results between pipelines
source: Russell, The CRAY-1 Computer System, CACM 1978

name: MMX
note: Integer only; registers aliased onto the x87 floating-point stack
source: Peleg & Weiser, MMX Technology Extension to the Intel Architecture, IEEE Micro 1996

name: SSE / SSE2
note: SSE2 is the x86-64 baseline: every 64-bit x86 CPU has at least 128-bit SIMD
source: Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manual, Vol. 1, ch. 10-11

name: AltiVec / VMX
note: 32 vector registers and a general permute (vperm) from the start
source: Diefendorff et al., AltiVec Extension to PowerPC Accelerates Media Processing, IEEE Micro 2000

name: NEON (Advanced SIMD)
ml_types: fp32, fp16, bf16, int8 dot (SDOT/UDOT, Armv8.2)
note: Mandatory in AArch64 (32 x 128-bit registers); every phone CPU has it
source: Arm Architecture Reference Manual for A-profile

name: AVX
note: 256-bit floating point only; VEX three-operand encoding
source: Intel SDM Vol. 1, ch. 14

name: AVX2 + FMA3
note: 256-bit integers, fused multiply-add, first x86 gather (vpgatherdd); x86-64-v3 baseline
source: Intel SDM Vol. 1, ch. 14

name: AVX-512
note: 32 zmm registers, masking on almost every instruction, compress/expand, conflict detection (CD) for scatter
source: Intel SDM Vol. 1, ch. 15; Intel Intrinsics Guide

name: AMX (TMUL)
matrix: 8 tiles of 16 rows x 64 bytes; TDPBF16PS: 16x32 bf16 times 32x16 into 16x16 fp32
note: width_bits is one 1 KB tile; a tile op is a small matrix multiply, not a lane-wise op
source: Intel SDM Vol. 1, ch. 20 (Intel AMX)

name: AVX10.2
ml_types: fp32, fp64, bf16, fp16, fp8 conversions, int8
first_silicon: announced for Nova Lake / Diamond Rapids (unconfirmed timing)
note: Converges AVX-512 features under one versioned ISA; the 2024 spec revision made 512-bit support mandatory on all cores
source: Intel AVX10.2 Architecture Specification (2024); press coverage of Nova Lake support (secondary)

name: SVE
ml_types: fp64, fp32, fp16, bf16, int8 dot
note: Hardware chooses 128-2048 bits; the same binary runs on all. width_bits is the architectural maximum. First-faulting loads vectorize while-loops
source: Stephens et al., The ARM Scalable Vector Extension, IEEE Micro 2017

name: SVE2
note: Armv9 baseline; brings NEON's integer/DSP coverage to the VLA model
source: Arm Architecture Reference Manual, SVE2 supplement

name: SME / SME2
matrix: ZA array SVL x SVL bytes; FMOPA outer product (16x16 fp32 tile at SVL 512)
note: Outer-product engine: two vectors in, a whole tile updated. width_bits is M4's streaming vector length
source: Arm SME documentation; Remke & Breuer, Hello SME! (arXiv:2409.18779)

name: RISC-V V 1.0
note: vsetvli returns how many elements this iteration may process; LMUL groups up to 8 registers. width_bits is the spec maximum VLEN
source: RISC-V V Vector Extension 1.0 specification (ratified 2021)

name: Hexagon HVX
ml_types: int8, int16, int32 (fp16/fp32 on newer versions)
note: Very wide fixed vectors on a VLIW DSP; the classic home of on-device int8 inference
source: Codrescu, Qualcomm Hexagon DSP: An Architecture Optimized for Mobile Multimedia and Communications (Hot Chips 2013); Hexagon HVX Programmer's Reference

name: CUDA SIMT warp
note: 32 threads x 32-bit = 1024 bits of lanes, programmed as scalar threads. Every load is a gather; coalescing makes contiguous ones cheap
source: Lindholm et al., NVIDIA Tesla: A Unified Graphics and Computing Architecture, IEEE Micro 2008

name: Tensor Cores (Volta)
matrix: 4x4x4 FMA per tensor core per clock; warp-level 16x16x16 (wmma)
note: The warp, not the thread, issues the matrix op
source: NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPU Architecture whitepaper (2017)

name: Tensor Cores (Hopper, wgmma)
matrix: warpgroup (128 threads) asynchronous MMA, operands from shared memory; TMA bulk copies
note: width_bits counts the 4 warps of a warpgroup x 1024
source: NVIDIA H100 Tensor Core GPU Architecture whitepaper (2022); PTX ISA wgmma

name: Tensor Cores (Blackwell, tcgen05)
ml_types: fp4 (NVFP4, MXFP4), fp6, fp8, fp16, bf16, tf32, int8
matrix: single-thread-issued UMMA, accumulators in Tensor Memory (TMEM), hardware block scaling
note: Accumulators leave the register file entirely; consumer Blackwell (sm_120) has no TMEM
source: NVIDIA Blackwell architecture technical brief; PTX ISA tcgen05; Colfax CUTLASS tutorials

name: AMD wavefront + MFMA
ml_types: fp64, fp32, fp16, bf16, fp8 (CDNA3), int8
matrix: Matrix Fused Multiply-Add (MFMA) instructions on CDNA
note: 64-wide wavefronts on CDNA (RDNA uses 32 or 64); the EXEC mask is the predication mechanism, visible in the ISA
source: AMD CDNA Instruction Set Architecture reference guides

name: TPU v1 MXU
note: 65,536 8-bit MACs. width_bits counts 256 x 256 x 8-bit weights held in the array
source: Jouppi et al., In-Datacenter Performance Analysis of a Tensor Processing Unit, ISCA 2017

name: TPU v2-v5 MXU
ml_types: bf16 (with fp32 accumulate), int8 on later parts
note: Training generation; bfloat16 introduced. width_bits counts 128 x 128 x 16-bit
source: Jouppi et al., A Domain-Specific Supercomputer for Training Deep Neural Networks, CACM 2020

name: TPU v6e / v7 MXU
matrix: 256 x 256 MACs per MXU (Trillium; Ironwood per secondary sources)
note: Google states the MXU grew for Trillium; the 256 x 256 size for v6e/v7 comes from secondary sources (unconfirmed)
source: Google Cloud blog, Introducing Trillium (2024); SemiAnalysis InferenceX glossary (secondary)

name: WebAssembly SIMD128
ml_types: fp32, fp64, int8-int64; relaxed-SIMD dot products
note: Portable 128-bit SIMD that maps to SSE or NEON underneath; the reason in-browser ML runtimes can vectorize
source: WebAssembly SIMD proposal (Phase 4/5, 2021)
